rules.name: Shannon entropy definition
preconditions: A logarithm base and discrete distribution are specified
rules.operation: Compute Shannon entropy from the active discrete distribution.
examples: A fair binary variable has larger entropy than a deterministic variable
counterexamples: Omitting the minus sign is invalid

rules.name: Chain rule for joint entropy
preconditions: The joint and conditional distributions are defined
rules.operation: Decompose joint entropy into marginal entropy plus conditional entropy.
examples: Joint uncertainty decomposes into uncertainty of one variable plus remaining uncertainty of the other after conditioning
counterexamples: Replacing conditional entropy by unconditional entropy is invalid in general

rules.name: Mutual information definition
preconditions: The joint distribution of X and Y is defined
rules.operation: Measure shared dependence through the standard entropy identity for mutual information.
examples: Mutual information measures shared dependence between random variables
counterexamples: Treating mutual information as signed and freely negative is invalid

rules.name: KL divergence nonnegativity seed
preconditions: The standard absolute-continuity hypotheses of the discrete setting hold
rules.operation: Use Gibbs-type inequality to keep KL divergence nonnegative.
examples: KL divergence measures directed discrepancy between distributions without becoming negative
counterexamples: Treating KL divergence as symmetric is invalid

rules.name: Channel capacity seed
rules.output_form: supremum of mutual information over admissible input distributions
preconditions: An admissible family of input distributions is specified for the channel
rules.operation: Define channel capacity as the maximal achievable mutual information rate in the basic channel model.
examples: Optimizing input statistics determines the maximal reliable information rate in the basic information-theoretic model
counterexamples: Fixing an arbitrary input distribution and calling its mutual information the capacity is invalid

rules.name: Conditional entropy rule
preconditions: The variables are interpreted in the standard discrete Shannon setting
rules.operation: Express conditional entropy as the difference between joint and marginal entropy.
examples: Conditioning can reduce uncertainty by accounting for side information carried by Y
counterexamples: Declaring conditional entropy negative in the ordinary discrete Shannon setting is invalid

rules.name: Data processing inequality seed
preconditions: The variables form the stated Markov chain in the standard information-theoretic sense
rules.operation: Forbid information increase under admissible post-processing.
examples: Post-processing cannot increase mutual information about the original source in the standard Markov-chain setting
counterexamples: Claiming deterministic processing always increases information is invalid

rules.name: Source coding theorem seed
rules.output_form: lossless coding length constrained by entropy and asymptotically achievable near it
preconditions: The standard asymptotic lossless source-coding setup is active
rules.operation: Use entropy as the fundamental asymptotic compression limit.
examples: Shannon entropy sets the fundamental compression scale for lossless source coding
counterexamples: Demanding arbitrarily short exact lossless codes below the entropy barrier is invalid in the standard asymptotic sense

rules.name: Channel coding theorem seed
rules.output_form: reliable transmission below capacity and impossibility above capacity in the standard asymptotic setting
preconditions: The standard noisy-channel asymptotic regime is active
rules.operation: Place the reliable-communication threshold at channel capacity.
examples: Channel capacity marks the asymptotic threshold between feasible and infeasible reliable transmission rates
counterexamples: Asserting arbitrarily small error at all rates above capacity is invalid

rules.name: Fano inequality seed
rules.output_form: error lower bound from conditional entropy and alphabet size
preconditions: A standard finite-alphabet decoding or classification setting is active
rules.operation: Lower-bound error probability using residual uncertainty.
examples: Fano-type bounds connect residual uncertainty with irreducible classification or decoding error
counterexamples: Treating zero mutual information as compatible with perfect decoding is invalid in the standard finite-alphabet setting

rules.name: Relative entropy chain decomposition seed
rules.output_form: marginal plus conditional divergence decomposition in the standard chain-rule setting
preconditions: The relevant joint, marginal, and conditional distributions are defined
rules.operation: Decompose joint relative entropy into staged contributions.
examples: Divergence across multistage models separates into stagewise information discrepancies
counterexamples: Treating KL divergence across coupled variables as always additively separable without conditioning terms is invalid

rules.name: Typical set seed
rules.input_form: long source sample from a discrete memoryless source
rules.output_form: high-probability typical set of near-entropy exponential size
preconditions: The standard asymptotic i.i.d. source setting is active
rules.operation: Concentrate long samples on a typical set with entropy-controlled size.
examples: Typicality explains why most long source outputs behave as though they carry roughly nH bits of information
counterexamples: Expecting every source word of a given length to be typical is invalid

rules.name: Rate-distortion seed
rules.output_form: minimum asymptotic rate for admissible distortion
preconditions: A source, reconstruction alphabet, and distortion measure are fixed
rules.operation: Quantify the least information rate needed for lossy reproduction under an allowed distortion level.
examples: Permitting more distortion lowers the minimal information rate needed for compression in lossy coding
counterexamples: Identifying lossless entropy directly with every lossy coding threshold is invalid

rules.name: Hypothesis testing divergence seed
preconditions: The standard asymptotic hypothesis-testing setting is active
rules.operation: Use divergence quantities to control asymptotic testing strength.
examples: Larger divergence supports exponentially stronger evidence separation between competing distribution models
counterexamples: Treating two identical distributions as asymptotically distinguishable with nontrivial exponent is invalid

rules.name: Fisher information geometry bridge seed
preconditions: A regular differentiable parametric model is fixed
rules.operation: Equip a statistical model family with a local metric from Fisher information.
examples: Parametric models can be compared locally by curvature-like information encoded in the Fisher metric
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary nondifferentiable model families as automatically carrying the same information-geometric metric is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
